subject: Enclave communication matrix and threat heatmap — RFI packet
messages:
From: Anita Roy <anita.roy@evergreenbank.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Chris Patel <c.patel@evergreenbank.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: enclave communication matrix + threat heatmap for RFI

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for taking our RFI. As part of Evergreen's vendor review we need: a concise communication matrix showing allowed egress/ingress between zones/enclaves, a compact network topology sketch (sanitized for non-prod), and a threat heatmap summarizing likely lateral movement paths and mitigations for our deployment model (VPC-peered, private control plane).

Deliverables we need by next Tuesday if possible:
- Single-sheet topology sketch (PNG) that shows control plane, tenant enclaves, sidecars, and egress choke points.
- A communication matrix (CSV/XLSX) mapping permitted flows (protocol/port) between components.
- A 1-page threat heatmap (PDF) highlighting top 5 prioritized attack paths with a short mitigation summary.

We will share this package with our network security and compliance teams; please avoid including internal hostnames or customer PII. Also include pointers to audit artifacts (flow logs, controlplane telemetry) and suggested evidence we can request during due diligence.

Let us know if you can provide a short 30-minute walkthrough after you send artifacts.

Thanks,
Anita
Anita Roy
Sr. Information Security Manager
Evergreen Bank

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anita Roy <anita.roy@evergreenbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: enclave communication matrix + threat heatmap for RFI

Hi Anita —

Appreciate the clear ask. We're attaching a sanitized package that should map directly to your checklist: topology_sketch_v2.png, threat_heatmap_v1.pdf, and control_matrix_revA.xlsx. High-level notes:

- Topology: shows a private control plane in a separate management VPC, tenant enclaves in user VPCs, sidecar proxies for inference traffic, an egress gateway cluster (bastionless), and optional dedicated/platinum paths for Dedicated customers. Diagram deliberately hides hostnames and customer identifiers.

- Communication matrix: row = source component, column = destination, with transport/protocol, typical ports, and where we enforce allowlists. We call out which flows are brokered by the control plane and which are strictly data-plane between sidecars and GPUs.

- Threat heatmap: prioritized attack paths (1–5). Examples: (1) compromised operator workstation -> control plane API misuse; (2) cross-tenant KV cache exposure during misconfigured quantization sharing; (3) lateral movement via sidecar debug endpoints. For each path we list corrective controls (IAM scope, mTLS, rate limiting, KV cache namespace separation, runtime sandboxing, automatic rollback).

Evidence pointers included in the control matrix worksheet: flow logs (VPC flow + sidecar telemetry), per-request provenance traces (control-plane request IDs), and retention policy pointers for audit logs. Links to the Drive folder and the Jira ticket are in the spreadsheet.

Two quick clarifications so we align the walkthrough:
1) Do you want the walkthrough focused on the prod-like architecture or the Dedicated offering (reserved capacity) where network plumbing differs?
2) Which team will attend — network ops, application security, or both?

We can do a 30-minute slot on Tue 29 Sep 14:00–14:30 PT; please confirm and we'll send a calendar invite with a short slide deck.

Best,

--
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineer, Security 
Redwood Inference
attachments: topology_sketch_v2.png (image/png), threat_heatmap_v1.pdf (application/pdf), control_matrix_revA.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Anita Roy <anita.roy@evergreenbank.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Chris Patel <c.patel@evergreenbank.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 08:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: enclave communication matrix + threat heatmap for RFI

Sofia —

Received and skimmed, looks good at first pass. A couple of small asks before the call:
- In the topology sketch, can you annotate which subnets are expected to be customer-controlled vs Redwood-managed (just a label, no CIDRs)?
- In the heatmap, could you add a short sentence for the control-plane guardrail that prevents operator API token reuse across tenants? We want that highlighted as a compensating control.
- For evidence, our auditors want the typical log retention windows (rollup by artifact type) and an example of a per-request provenance trace (redacted). If you can drop those into the Drive folder ahead of the meeting, that will speed us up.

Attendees for the call: network ops lead (me), security engineer (Chris). Please confirm the 14:00 PT slot and provide a meeting link.

Thanks,
Anita

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anita Roy <anita.roy@evergreenbank.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: enclave communication matrix + threat heatmap for RFI

Hi Anita —

Thanks for the review and the clarifying points. We've updated the artifacts in the Drive folder:
- topology_sketch_v2_annotated.png — added "Redwood-managed" vs "Customer-controlled" labels (no IPs).
- threat_heatmap_v1.1.pdf — added the sentence under control-plane guardrails re: operator token scoping and rotation cadence.
- control_matrix_revA_with_retention.xlsx — added an evidence sheet listing retention windows by artifact type and a redacted per-request provenance trace (example request ID: rwi-evg-20260929-zzxx; timeline removed).

I've included a short 6-slide deck in the folder that we will share during the walkthrough covering: architecture overview, top 5 attack paths, mapped mitigations, evidence pointers, and recommended due-diligence checklist.

Meeting: Tue 29 Sep, 14:00 PT (we're using Zoom). Invite sent separately; raw meeting link: https://zoom.us/j/999-111-2222?pwd=example

If Anita/Chris need additional artifacts (e.g., SOC2 control mappings or packet-level flow samples), let us know and we can prepare an evidence packet for the next gate.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Security Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference
